assets.content:
Subject: A confirmation page can be the conversion goal
Preview text: If signup ends there, Plausible already has the pageview, so no site code is needed.

Hi there,

Plausible Analytics lets you turn a completed trial signup into a conversion goal, then see which referrer sources and entry pages brought those conversions. That gives you more context than a topline signup total or rate.

First, check how signup completion appears on your site—not simply whether someone visited the signup page.

If completion reaches a dedicated confirmation page, you can create or review a pageview goal for that page. Plausible collects pageviews automatically, so this route needs no site code changes. If there is no distinct completion page, assess a custom event instead.

Once conversions are recorded, the dashboard can show the conversion count and rate, referrer sources, entry pages and pages where people converted.

The official guide explains both goal types so you can decide which one represents a completed trial signup correctly.

Inspect the goal-conversions guide →

- the Plausible Analytics team

brief.reader_segment: Small SaaS website owner measuring signup conversion
brief.promise: Plausible can make completed trial signups a conversion goal, then show which referrer sources and entry pages produced those conversions.
brief.orientation: Plausible Analytics is a web analytics tool that lets a small SaaS owner track trial signups as goals and inspect the traffic behind them in one dashboard.
brief.arc: Introduce Plausible through one useful action: define or verify the signup goal, inspect its source and landing-page context, then consult the official setup guide.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email is sufficient because the requested outcome is narrow. It should move directly from the reader's measurement question to a conditional setup step and a read-only documentation CTA, without adding pricing, migration, privacy, benchmarks or performance claims.

emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the official guide and determine whether their trial-signup completion should be tracked or reviewed as a Plausible goal.
emails.single_idea: Define the completed trial signup—not merely a visit to the signup page—as a Plausible goal, then filter the dashboard by that goal to see the referrer sources and entry pages associated with conversions.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.why_it_fails: A topline conversion rate alone does not identify which sources or entry pages brought the visitors who completed signup.
emails.mechanism: First check how signup completion is represented. If it reaches a dedicated confirmation page, create or verify a pageview goal for that page without changing site code; otherwise, use the official guide to assess a custom event. After the first recorded conversion, select the goal in the Goals section to filter the dashboard and inspect its referrer sources, entry pages and converting pages.
emails.belief_shift: Before: signup measurement is only a total or rate. After: a correctly defined completion goal can be used to examine where converting visits originated and entered the site.
must_not_say: Do not presume the reader currently uses Plausible, Google Analytics or any other analytics tool.
Do not presume a dedicated confirmation page exists; present the pageview-goal path conditionally.
Do not claim Plausible will increase signups or conversion rate, or reuse Plausible's own measured lift as an expected outcome.
Do not present Plausible's published conversion figures as a benchmark for the reader's site.
Do not presume traffic volume, privacy compliance status, launch history, payment failures or trial-to-paid performance.
Do not imply that signup-goal tracking diagnoses billing failures, in-product trial behavior or paid conversion.
Do not broaden the email into pricing, migration, privacy, uptime, integrations, funnels or testimonials.

Plausible can only record a paid conversion if the owner sends it as a backend event, revenue attribution sits on the Business plan, and the ledger contains nothing about in-trial product usage or billing, so the measurement stops at.

The 2.65% to 4.80% lift (E11) came from Plausible editing its own homepage, not from installing Plausible; the product locates entry pages and drop-off steps and the owner still has to make the change and re-measure.
emails.objection: Setting up conversion tracking may sound like it requires development work; clarify that a pageview goal needs no code when signup ends on a dedicated confirmation page, while other completion patterns may require a custom event.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the site's completed trial signup should use a pageview goal or a custom event, and whether an existing goal represents completion correctly.
emails.next_step_value: The guide explains the two core goal types and how configured goals expose conversion counts, rates, referrer sources, entry pages and converting pages in the dashboard.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide does not configure the site, validate a live implementation or establish what conversion rate the business should expect.
emails.subject_strategy: Name the concrete measurement task—understanding where trial signups come from—without promising growth or using a generic analytics claim.

brief.voice_notes: Use short, declarative sentences and product terms such as “goal,” “referrer source,” “entry page” and “dashboard.” Avoid hype and the phrase “Get started.”
